headline: Approved Riverwalk North public access alignment, new motorized scooter rules, and a Greater Portland Transit District student pass agreement.
summary: Three orders on final reading included bid awards for a fire department air compressor and an aerial bucket truck. A grant application for a pedestrian project at Hannaford Drive was endorsed, and Melissa Littlehale was confirmed as tax collector. Replacement pump station doors and a forest mulcher rental passed first reading.
decisions: Approved Orders 2026-81, 2026-82, and 2026-83 on second and final reading, 7-0.
Failed 2-5 to add a Munroe Avenue bus route to the transit pass order and send it to committee.
Approved Order 2026-84, the student transit pass agreement with Greater Portland Transit District, 5-2.
Approved Resolve 2026-15 endorsing the public access alignment for the Riverwalk North project, 7-0.
Approved changing the date in the Order 2026-85 tax collector appointment from April 1, 2020, to April 1, 2021, by show of hands.
Confirmed the appointment of Melissa Littlehale as Tax Collector, 7-0.
Endorsed the PACTS 2026 grant application for a pedestrian intersection improvement project at Hannaford Drive, 6-0.
Amended Chapter 310 Vehicles and Traffic of the Code of Ordinances on motorized scooters, 7-0.
Approved the first of two readings for purchase of replacement pump station doors, by show of hands.
Approved the first of two readings for forest mulcher rental and an amendment to the Annual Vendor List, by show of hands.

WESTBROOK CITY COUNCIL 
REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES 
MONDAY, AUGUST 3, 2026 AT 6:00 PM  
WESTBROOK HIGH SCHOOL (ROOM 114) 
125 STROUDWATER ST.  
 
 
  
 
 
I. LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT STATEMENT 
Meeting called to order at 6:00pm by City Council President Jennifer Munro. City Clerk Ellis Ledoux read the 
City Council Land Acknowledgment statement into the record. 
 
  
II. ROLL CALL 
City Councilors Present: Michael Shaughnessy (At-Large, Vice-President), Brian McCambridge (Ward 1), Anna 
A. Turcotte (Ward 3), Victor Chau (Ward 2), Amy Faulkingham (Ward 4), Jennifer Munro (Ward 5, President), 
Gary Rairdon (At-Large) 
 
City Councilors Absent: None 
 
Other City Officials Present: Eric Dudley (Director of Engineering & Public Services), Jennie Franceschi 
(Assistant City Administrator), Angela Holmes (City Administrator), Laura King (Interim Finance Director/Tax 
Collector), Sean Lally (Police Chief), Ellis Ledoux (City Clerk), David Morse (Mayor), Robyn Saunders (Project 
Manager), Stephen Sloan (Fire Chief), Monique Cornett (Director of Economic Development), Melissa Littlehale 
(Tax Collector), Cameron Ferrante (Legal Counsel), Katherine Kelley (Wastewater Division Manager), Dr. Lancia 
(Superintendent of Schools), Andrea Mancuso (School Committee, Ward 4), Erin Cavallaro (School Committee, 
Ward 2) 
 
  
III. PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE  
 
City Council President Munro led all present in the Pledge of Allegiance. 
  
IV. APPROVAL OF MINUTES  
 
There were no meeting minutes for approval 
  
V. MAYOR'S MESSAGE 
Mayor Morse read his message into the record. The snippets are included below: 
 
• Westbrook police department is hosting a National Night Out Celebration from 5:00pm – 7:00pm 
tomorrow night (August 4, 2026) at St Anthony’s Church 268 Brown Street 
• Recognized Barry Dodd for his 12 years of dedication and hard work as the city’s Digital Creative 
Services Administrator 
• Highlighted Order 2026-87 for improvements to the pedestrian crosswalks at William Clarke Dr. and 
Hannaford Dr. 
• Applications are now open for the Westbrook Food Security Grant Program
VI. CITY COUNCIL MESSAGES 
City Council President Munro opened the floor for City Council messages. Councilors provided the following 
updates:  
 
President Munro mentioned that a car approached and passed a car on E. Bridge St. Please slow down and be 
safe. Kids are out of school at this time of year.  
 
  
VII. STUDENT REPRESENTATIVE UPDATE 
There was no Student Representative update. 
 
  
VIII. PUBLIC COMMENT 
City Council President Munro opened the floor for the first public comment portion of this meeting. The 
following individuals spoke: Larry McWilliams (383 Austin St.), Barry Dodd (former Westbrook employee) 
comment read into the record. 
 
  
IX. UNFINISHED BUSINESS 
There was no unfinished business for consideration.  
 
  
X. ORDERS OF THE DAY (SECOND AND FINAL READING)

Order 2026-82. Authorizing Award of Bid for Replacement Fire Department SCBA Air Compressor

spoke

spoke: Larry McWilliams (383 Austin St), Angela Holmes (City Administrator), Eric Dudley (Director of 
Public Services & Engineering), Joyce Van Lawsen (41 Monroe Avenue) 
Motion carried. Order 2026-81 through 2026–83 adopted. (Vote 7-0)

Motion to amend the order to include the bus route on Munroe Ave be sent to a committee for
